title: Bud Rankin's family and rehearsals at Moreau gigs
summary: The Rankin family hosted rehearsals in their living room. Bud's father had the first taxicab in town. A violinist from St. Joe who worked with Coleman Hawkins joined the Moreau gigs.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Anyhow, on these gigs sometimes -- I don't want to forget this -- Bud Rankin, may I dwell on him for a minute?
Yes.
It's musical. I mean what I'm talking about him is musical.
Yes, anything. Sure, anything related to music.
Well, his father had the first taxicab in the town and they were a very well-respected family.
In Jefferson City?
Jeff City. See, that's your problem. You say Jefferson City, you know. That's the way it is but it's plain old Jeff.
Yeah. Well, I've never heard that before.
JTHOMAS (1)
And that was our rehearsal spot. We'd got to the Rankin's to rehearse.
In the garage or something?
No, no. In the living room.
In the house, oh.

Yeah. They were doing all right there and very well respected people. And he would call in a fellow from St. Joe and he played violin and he used to work with Coleman Hawkins and his-name-is and I can't think of his name offhand right now but I will sometime later on.
That's where Coleman Hawkins came from.
St. Joe, yeah.
How far away would that be?
St. Joe from Jeff City? Oh, I don't know. St. Joe is around Liberty, Kansas City, maybe another 145 miles.
Quite a long way away.
Yeah. So he would come over and do these gigs with us at Moreau. Now we had the dedication and the capital to come up and we would ... (tape cut off)
